purpose: Symlinks inside tree artifacts (declare_directory outputs): TreeArtifactValue.visitTree (skyframe/TreeArtifactValue.java:548-592) follows every symlink below a tree root, and ActionOutputMetadataStore.constructTreeArtifactValueFromFilesystem (skyframe/ActionOutputMetadataStore.java:245-316) makes the regular files reached the tree's children at their apparent paths (directories are no children; entries reached through a link are never chmod'ed); invalid links fail with reportOutputTreeArtifactErrors (SkyframeActionExecutor.java:1556-1569). Shapes: rules_oci 2.x image.sh with bazel_features.rules.permits_treeartifact_uplevel_symlinks (relative up-level links from blobs/sha256 to a layer and to an input image tree's blobs), links inside the tree, chains, directory links inside and out of the tree, links to source inputs (plain and executable), an empty-directory link, a link to another output of the same action, an absolute link to a host file, absolute links through the action's working directory (sandboxed and unsandboxed), dangling relative and absolute links, a link to a device, a link loop, directory cycles, a link to an undeclared source; consumers: Args expansion and reads in a sandboxed and an unsandboxed action, ctx.actions.symlink of a tree, `run` through the runfiles tree, `test` with the tree in the test's runfiles. Motivation: every rules_oci oci_image on ~/code failed natively (`symlinks inside tree artifacts are not supported by the native profile`; TEST-SURVEY L1).

reference.environment: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME/TMPDIR private LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8; default registry (bcr.bazel.build); one fresh copy of the fixture workspace per case (platforms extracted from tests/fixtures/label_repo_name/platforms_archive.json); default spawn strategy = processwrapper-sandbox on this host (no usable linux-sandbox)

normalization: <WS> = the case's workspace copy; <OB> = the genuine output base; <CACHE> = the native cache; elapsed times <T>. Outputs: genuine --show_result's paths (bazel-bin = bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin), native the LABEL<TAB>PATH result lines with the path below the published action's outputs/ directory; a file is [mode, contents], a tree {followed: [path, x or -, size, sha256 prefix] of every regular file reached following symlinks (a file equal to the host's /bin/sh as host/host-bin-sh), raw: [path, l/d/f, link target] without following}. The consumers' listings (`.txt`) print the Args expansion of the tree (TreeArtifactValue children) and the followed files with their executable bit as the action sees them; `.raw` the staged entries' unfollowed types.
comparison (tests/tree_symlinks.rs, live: MATCH: success equal; a failing case's first genuine ERROR message (after its location) is contained in native stderr, or for ELOOP messages (which name genuine's absolute path) its parts around the path; built cases: every `.txt` listing (mode and contents) and every tree's followed view equal; `run`: the program's stdout equal; `test`: stdout (test logs and summary, times <T>) equal. DECLARED_DIVERGENCE: native fails with the recorded message. Not compared (evidence, docs/TREE_SYMLINKS.md): `.raw` listings and trees' raw views.
genuine_key_findings: Every link that resolves is followed: the tree's children (the Args expansion) are the regular files reached, at the links' paths - files behind relative up-level links (rules_oci's blobs/sha256/<layer> -> ../../../layer.tar and links into an input image tree's blobs), links inside the tree, chains, files below directory links inside and out of the tree, links to source inputs, to another output of the same action, an absolute link to a host file (/bin/sh) and, unsandboxed, an absolute link into the execution root. Directories are no children: a link to an empty directory adds nothing.

Through a link a consumer sees the resolved file's content and mode: links to outputs and to files of the tree are executable (0555 after the action), a link to a plain source file (0644) is not, to an executable source (0755) is.

The published tree keeps the links as the action made them (`bazel-bin/pkg/uplevel/blobs/sha256/layer -> ../../../layer.tar`); a processwrapper-sandboxed consumer sees every child as a symlink to its execution-root path, an unsandboxed one the producer's own links.

`error while validating output tree artifact pkg/T: child y is a dangling symbolic link` for dangling relative and absolute links and for an absolute link into the action's sandbox (gone before the outputs are collected); `child null has an unsupported type` for a link to /dev/null; `[unix_jni.cc:382] <path> (Too many levels of symbolic links)` for a link loop and for directory cycles (sub/up -> .., self -> .) after the kernel's 40-link limit; then `TreeSymlinks pkg/T failed: not all outputs were created or valid`.
A relative link to a source file that is not an input of the action resolves (genuine reads the tree in its execution root, where every source is reachable).
`run` reads the tree through the runfiles tree (a link to the tree directory); `test` stages the tree's children into the test's runfiles; both read the linked files' contents.
known_divergences: Publication materializes links: a native published tree holds the resolved files (store inodes with the resolved file's executable bits) and real directories, never symlinks, because a native output lives in its action's own cache entry, where a relative link would not resolve; `readlink`/`find -type l` see regular files (the raw views).
Consumers stage tree files as read-only hardlinks like every native input (genuine's sandbox stages symlinks to execution-root paths): the raw views differ, the followed listings are equal.
A native directory cycle fails at the link that closes it (genuine after 40 levels): ELOOP messages name a shorter path.
Native trees keep their empty directories (staged and published), a pre-existing difference: genuine's consumers see only the children.
Declared divergence: a relative link to a file that is not an input of the action (undeclared, undeclared_consumer).
Native needs --experimental-builtin-modules for the exec cases (the default host platform's @platforms//host); it is passed in every native case; native prints its own result format.

bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/pkg/show_uple:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

listing() {
  tree="$1"
  shift
  echo "expanded:"
  for child in "$@"; do
    echo "  ${child#"$tree"/}"
  done
  echo "files:"
  (cd "$tree" && find -L . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort) | while read -r rel; do
    rel="${rel#./}"
    if [ -x "$tree/$rel" ]; then x=x; else x=-; fi
    size=$(wc -c < "$tree/$rel")
    sum=$(sha256sum < "$tree/$rel" | cut -c1-16)
    if [ "$rel" = "sh" ] && cmp -s "$tree/$rel" /bin/sh; then sum=host-bin-sh; size=host; fi
    echo "  $rel $x $size $sum"
  done
}

status=0
check() {
  if [ "$(cat "$tree/$1")" = "$2" ]; then echo "ok $1"; else echo "mismatch $1"; status=1; fi
}
tree="pkg/uplevel"
listing "$tree"
check "blobs/sha256/layer" "layer-bytes"
check "index.json" "{}"
exit $status
